title: lore new --template <name>.md double-appends the extension and its own not-found hint tells the user to create the doubled file
description:
Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-18, measured against the installed 0.7.0 binary. Independently
re-verified here against dev at HEAD, via `bun run src/cli.ts` in a throwaway bundle -- STILL
PRESENT, not already fixed.

THE DEFECT: `--template <name>.md` double-appends the extension and fails, even when the exact
file exists.

  # .lore/templates/feature.md exists
  lore new adr "Probe" --template feature       # OK
  lore new adr "Probe" --template feature.md    # error: template "feature.md" not found in .lore/templates/
                                                 # hint: create .lore/templates/feature.md.md

Confirmed here byte-for-byte, including the doubled-extension hint.

ROOT CAUSE, located: src/commands/new.ts:354-381, `resolveTemplate`. The profile-declared source
strips a trailing `.md` before use:

  const declared = profile.types.get(type)?.template?.replace(/\.md$/i, "");
  const base = parsed.template ?? declared ?? type;

but the CLI-flag source, `parsed.template`, does NOT go through the same `.replace(/\.md$/i, "")` --
it is used verbatim. `templateCandidates(base)` then appends `.md` unconditionally
(`${TEMPLATES_DIR}/${candidate}.md`), so `--template feature.md` builds
`.lore/templates/feature.md.md`. The not-found error at line 372-378 reuses the same un-stripped
`parsed.template` to build both the message and the hint, which is why the hint itself tells the
user to create a doubly-extensioned file:

  `create ${TEMPLATES_DIR}/${parsed.template}.md, or omit --template to use the built-in`

WHY THE HINT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN A BARE PAPERCUT: it does not just fail on the extensioned
spelling -- it actively tells the user to create `.lore/templates/feature.md.md`, which would
"fix" the immediate error while leaving a wrongly-named file behind for the next reader to wonder
about. A user who follows the hint literally ends up worse off than one who got no hint at all.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: apply the same `.replace(/\.md$/i, "")` to `parsed.template` that
`declared` already gets, before it becomes `base` -- both spellings then resolve to the same file,
and the not-found error/hint should use the stripped `base` (or an explicitly re-derived name)
rather than the raw flag value, so a future case can't reintroduce the doubled-extension hint even
if the lookup itself gets fixed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: --template feature and --template feature.md resolve to the same .lore/templates/feature.md file when it exists.
The not-found error and its hint never suggest a doubled extension, for either spelling of --template.
A regression test covers both spellings against the same fixture file.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.
